title: More Ships Attacked Near an Important Oil Waterway
summary:
The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow waterway in the Middle East. Many ships carry oil through it to the rest of the world. Since the war between the US and Israel and Iran began, ships there have been attacked.

Between October 5 and October 11, twelve ships were reported attacked. That is the most in one week since the war started. These numbers are approximate.

Experts say Iran is attacking ships to try to control the waterway. The US military is helping more tankers travel through safely. It says ships are still moving through the strait. When one container ship sank this week, all 21 crew members were safely evacuated.

The attacks have slowed oil shipments. About 12.6 million barrels a day passed through on October 13, according to the data firm Kpler. Before the war, it was about 17 million.
why_it_matters: Oil from this waterway is used to make fuel, so problems there can affect gas prices around the world.

Many countries send oil by ship through this waterway to the rest of the world.
When fewer ships can pass safely, less oil reaches other countries.
